## Chapter Summary

Many analytical questions need more than grouping. A CASE expression classifies each row by conditions tested in order, and its ELSE decides what happens to rows that meet none of them. Placed inside an aggregate, CASE turns categories into columns, which is conditional aggregation, the SQL counterpart of a PivotTable. SQLite stores dates as text, and its date functions work on that text. strftime formats a date into a period such as a year and month, and date moves a date with modifiers such as start of month. julianday turns a date into a number of days, so that the difference between two dates is a subtraction. Date functions return text, except julianday, so their results must be compared with text or converted with CAST.

A window function calculates across a set of rows but keeps every row. PARTITION BY divides the rows into groups without collapsing them, ORDER BY sets their order, and a frame such as ROWS BETWEEN 11 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW decides which rows each calculation uses. Ranking functions, such as ROW_NUMBER and RANK, number the rows. Aggregate functions over an ordered window produce running and moving totals, such as year-to-date and trailing twelve-month figures. LAG and LEAD return values from earlier and later rows, such as the same month a year before. Window functions are calculated after grouping, so they can work on grouped results, but a WHERE clause cannot filter on them without a derived table or a common table expression.

A common table expression names a subquery at the start of a query with WITH, so that a long analysis reads as a series of steps that can each be checked on their own. A view saves a query in the database under a name. It stores the query rather than its result, so it always reflects the current data, and it is written only into the working copy, never into the downloaded file.

Applied to the controller's question, these tools produced a monthly measure of labor hours per standard hour, smoothed over a trailing twelve months and saved as a view. The payroll classified with CASE tied to the ledger's charge to the cent. The measure rose steadily through fiscal 2025 and fiscal 2026, and the share of overtime rose with it. Work orders took more than twice as long to complete. The ranking of work centers also exposed a pattern in the time records: far more hours than planned at the end of the routing, and far fewer at its start. That pattern is for the auditors of Chapter 12 to test.
